Hi Priya,

We're moving into the final security review for the inference platform line item and need concrete answers and evidence for a few items around key management and transport security before the procurement committee meets next week. High level asks: 

- Do you support customer-provided keys (BYOK) for hosted workloads and for private deployments? Please describe the lifecycle and who ultimately controls key material.
- For HSM-backed keys: vendor support, FIPS level, and whether attestation/CSR artifacts are available.
- Key rotation policy: supported rotation modes (automatic vs manual), default intervals, and how previous key versions are retained for decryption.
- TLS: supported versions/ciphers, mutual TLS support for connector endpoints, and certificate rotation cadence.
- Evidence: any attestation letter, runbook, or sample audit log extract we can include in the RFP appendix.

If you can send a short technical summary and attach anything we can drop into the RFP appendix, that would be ideal.

Thanks,

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@upstart.ai>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: Request: BYOK provisioning & TLS attestation — Upstart RFP

Jordan — providing the technical summary below. Attaching: Redwood_BYOK_Workflow.pdf, BYOK_Attestation_Letter.pdf, FIPS1403-compatibility-summary.pdf (see attachments referenced in the thread).

1) BYOK support and custody model
- Hosted (Redwood API): We support customer-managed keys via envelope encryption. Customers may supply a customer master key (CMK) in their cloud KMS (AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault) and configure a customer key alias in their account. Redwood encrypts model and runtime secrets with a per-tenant data key that is wrapped by the CMK (Key-Wrapping). 
- Private (VPC/on-prem): For Private deployments we support HSM-backed CMKs (Thales nShield or AWS CloudHSM) controlled by the customer. In Private mode the customer controls the HSM and the root key material — Redwood operators do not have access to the unwrapped CMK.
- Ownership: For Hosted, customers maintain the CMK in their cloud account (BYOK). For Private, key material remains under customer control in customer-managed HSMs. In both cases the wrapped data keys are stored encrypted; unwrapping for in-memory usages is performed only by the runtime component authorized by the customer's key policy.

2) HSM / FIPS attestation
- We validate HSM compatibility with FIPS 140-2 and 140-3 where applicable. For Private deployments customers may use FIPS 140-2 Level 3 modules (Thales nShield) or equivalent certified appliances. 
- Attestation artifacts: we can provide an attestation letter describing the HSM configuration used for Private deployments and a redacted HSM CSR/attestation summary for Hosted scenarios where a managed HSM is used. (See attached BYOK_Attestation_Letter.pdf.)

3) Key rotation & versioning
- Rotation modes: automatic rotation (scheduled) and customer-driven rotation via KMS API.
- Defaults: data keys (ephemeral per-session) rotate on every session/token by default; envelope CMKs are rotated on customer schedule. We recommend a 90-day rotation cadence for re-wrapping workloads but Redwood will not rotate a customer-managed CMK without the customer's explicit action or a mutually agreed policy in the contract.
- Backward compatibility: Redwood retains previous wrapped key versions for decryption of historical objects; the runtime consults key metadata to select the correct unwrapping key version. Keys are retained per customer retention policy; typical retention for wrapped keys is aligned with your data retention SLA and is configurable.

4) TLS / transport security
- Supported TLS versions: TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 (1.3 preferred).
- Cipher suites: we support modern ECDHE-based suites (e.g., TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384, ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256 for 1.2 compatibility).
- mTLS: Mutual TLS is supported for private connector endpoints and for Dedicated/Private deployments. For Hosted public API endpoints we support client certificate authentication via short-lived tokens and can enable mTLS for enterprise accounts on request (requires cert provisioning and CA trust exchange).
- Certificate rotation: Certificates for service endpoints are rotated automatically (managed certificates) on a 90-day cadence; customer-managed certificates for mTLS are rotated per customer schedule — we provide hooks to validate cert chains and a rotation API to upload replacement certs.

5) Auditability & evidence
- Audit logs: key unwrap/cryptographic operations are logged with request id, principal, operation, and timestamp. Logs can be exported to your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog/CloudWatch) or delivered via customer-configurable log sinks for Private deployments. Retention and export formats are configurable.
- Pen-testing & compliance: Redwood publishes summary results for periodic penetration tests and SOC 2 reports; we can provide redacted logs and an attestation letter for inclusion in the RFP appendix (attached).

If you want, Marissa and I can run a staged BYOK injection test in our sandbox with you and capture an audit-log trace for the appendix.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Security, Redwood Inference

Rishi — this is very helpful. A couple quick clarifications before we include the text in the RFP appendix: 

1) For Hosted BYOK, can you confirm whether Redwood performs any automated CMK rotation on behalf of the customer if configured in Redwood Console? We need to state whether control plane can trigger rewraps.
2) For the HSM attestation letter: will the artifact include the HSM vendor, firmware version, and a redacted serial that we can reference in our audit? Upstart's auditors need a minimal set of identifiers.
3) For logs: what is the default retention for key unwrap events in Hosted and in Dedicated? We may need 1 year of retention for the RFP.

Also — can you confirm whether mTLS for hosted endpoints is available in the next 30 days for an enterprise pilot?

Thanks,
Jordan

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-19T10:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: BYOK provisioning & TLS attestation — Upstart RFP

Jordan — answers inline: 

> 1) For Hosted BYOK, can you confirm whether Redwood performs any automated CMK rotation on behalf of the customer if configured in Redwood Console?

Short answer: no automatic rotation of a customer-managed CMK without explicit customer approval. Background: Redwood can trigger re-wraps of data keys when you request a key rotation via the console/API; we will not rotate a CMK that lives in your cloud KMS without an explicit API call from your KMS account or a mutually agreed contract clause. We can, however, automate re-wrapping policies for data keys derived from a CMK if you opt into that managed workflow.

> 2) For the HSM attestation letter: will the artifact include the HSM vendor, firmware version, and a redacted serial that we can reference in our audit?

Yes — for Private deployments the attestation letter will include vendor and firmware version and a redacted identifier. For Hosted managed HSMs we can provide a compatibility/attestation summary that references the managed HSM provider and a redacted attestation token. The attached BYOK_Attestation_Letter.pdf is formatted for RFP inclusion.

> 3) For logs: what is the default retention for key unwrap events in Hosted and in Dedicated?

Defaults: Hosted: 90 days (configurable up to 2 years with an enterprise add-on). Dedicated/Private: configurable; default ship is 365 days for audit logs. We will include the log export snippet for your appendix.

mTLS pilot: we can enable mTLS for Hosted enterprise pilot within 30 days — requires CA exchange and a short integration window. Marissa will coordinate scheduling.

I'll also drop the single-file RFP appendix (attestations + short answers) into the Drive link and share the HubSpot record.

Best,
Priya
